predecessors.name: Swiss Confederation
predecessors.text: the thirteen old cantons and their subject lands, which the French overran on 5 March 1798

successors.name: Swiss Confederation
successors.text: the cantons restored by the Act of Mediation

ledger.x: 1798: the seat moves from Aarau to Lucerne (infobox 'Lucerne (1798-1799)'); the page gives years only.
1799: the seat moves from Lucerne to Bern (infobox 'Bern (1799-1803)'); the page gives years only.
October 1799: the Allies leave Swiss soil.
October 1799: the Russians have been beaten and Zurich is back (see the Austrian contest_end).
19 February 1803: the Mediation Confederation takes the cantons.

wars.name: French invasion of Switzerland
wars.outcome: The Confederacy collapsed on 5 March 1798; the Republic was proclaimed on 12 April; Schwyz surrendered on 4 May and a cease-fire of 13 May ended the rising, the rebel cantons merging into one.

wars.name: War of the Second Coalition in Switzerland
wars.outcome: French victory at the Second Battle of Zurich (25-26 September 1799); the last Allied troops left on 15 October; Russia withdrew from the Coalition; the war 'greatly weakened the Helvetic Republic'.

wars.name: Stecklikrieg
wars.outcome: Civil war of 1802 after the French withdrawal; the Helvetic government 'took refuge in Lausanne' and Napoleon summoned both sides to Paris, leading to the Act of Mediation of 19 February 1803.

certainty.note: Cantonal limits and the Rhine and Jura frontiers with France are administrative and long fixed; the exceptions are the front of 1799 (eastern Switzerland and Zurich, held by the Allies for months) and the Valais, whose status was unsettled…
